document.abstract: In order to obtain data on deionization times of high-voltage fault-arc paths the Bonneville Power Administration has made oscillographic and photographic records of electrical arcs produced on 115- and 230-kv buses with current magnitudes up to 25,000 amp. Speeds of 4000 frames/sec were used. Since the arcing times were very brief (0.1 to 0.01 sec), camera timing was critical. This, and estimation of the actinic value of the self-luminous arc, were the principal problems encountered. Another problem was photography of a self-luminous arc of high intensity against a background which must also appear in the picture when the arc is out.
